phases.title: Phase 1: Linear Foundations & Hardware Calibration
phases.description: Complexity calibration, memory hierarchy (64B cache lines, contiguous layouts), prefix/suffix reasoning, two pointers, sliding window invariants, binary search variants, heaps/top-K, monotonic stacks, and bit manipulation.

phases.title: Phase 2: Hierarchical Structures, Topologies & Compilers
phases.description: Tree recursion contracts, subtree post-order DP, BST ordering, Tries, graph BFS/DFS, Disjoint Set Union (DSU), topological sorting, backtracking with dedup/pruning, and memoization bridges.

phases.title: Phase 3: Advanced Optimization, Range Queries & Flows
phases.description: Interval/Bitmask/Tree DP, Segment Trees with lazy propagation, Fenwick Trees, Tarjan's bridges & SCC, Dinic's max-flow, hardware cache locality, Cuckoo/Robin Hood hashing, and string automata (KMP, BPE).

phases.title: Phase 4: Systems & AI-Infrastructure Domain Specialization
phases.description: Cache architectures (ARC, 2Q, Clock-Pro, PagedAttention), lock-free concurrency (SPSC/MPMC ring buffers, work-stealing deques), HNSW vector proximity graphs, ML compiler DAG schedulers, Blelloch parallel scan, streaming sketches, and Buddy/Slab allocators.

patterns.name: Complexity calibration
patterns.recognitionCues: Any problem with 'efficient' + a large n stated
patterns.constraintTriggers: n in constraints
patterns.coreIdea: Derive acceptable TC from n BEFORE designing anything; eliminate approaches that cannot fit
patterns.dataStructures: None  -  pure reasoning
patterns.failureModes: Assuming O(n^2) passes at n=10^5; ignoring hash/recursion constants; never doing this step
patterns.canonicalExamples: Every single problem
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Latency budgets; SLO thresholds; batch-size selection

patterns.name: Frequency/counting + hashing
patterns.recognitionCues: 'anagram','k most frequent','duplicates','count of','appears more than once'
patterns.constraintTriggers: values bounded or hashable; n up to 10^6
patterns.coreIdea: Replace repeated scans with one pass building counts; hash the KEY that captures the invariant
patterns.dataStructures: hash map, count array, bucket array
patterns.failureModes: Counting when positions matter; wrong key granularity; using set when count needed
patterns.canonicalExamples: Group anagrams, top-K, majority element, first unique character
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Hot-key detection, metric counters, histogram-based alerting

patterns.name: Prefix/suffix reasoning
patterns.recognitionCues: 'subarray sum','range query','product except self','subarrays satisfying condition'
patterns.constraintTriggers: static array, multiple queries, O(n) target
patterns.coreIdea: Precompute cumulative info so any range is O(1); prefix+hash converts a condition into a lookup
patterns.dataStructures: prefix array, hash map (prefix -> count or prefix -> first-index)
patterns.failureModes: Forgetting prefix[0]=0; using seen-set instead of count-map; applying to non-additive functions
patterns.canonicalExamples: Range sums, balanced subarrays, product except self, 2D regions
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Rolling aggregates, cumulative metrics, event-log windows

patterns.name: Two pointers (opposite ends)
patterns.recognitionCues: sorted or sortable input; 'pair/triplet sums to'; 'maximum area between'
patterns.constraintTriggers: sorted or O(n log n) sort acceptable
patterns.coreIdea: Move the pointer that provably cannot improve the answer; prove no valid pair is skipped
patterns.dataStructures: two indices into the same array
patterns.failureModes: Moving the wrong pointer; skipping duplicates incorrectly; not proving the discard
patterns.canonicalExamples: Two Sum II, 3Sum, Container With Most Water
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Merging sorted shard scans; two-way join on sorted data

patterns.name: Two pointers (same direction / read-write)
patterns.recognitionCues: 'in place','remove elements','partition','k-th from end'
patterns.constraintTriggers: O(1) extra space required; array mutation allowed
patterns.coreIdea: Separate a slow write-index from a fast read-index; maintain a region invariant
patterns.dataStructures: two indices, optional dummy node for lists
patterns.failureModes: Overwriting needed elements; not stating the region invariant; off-by-one
patterns.canonicalExamples: Remove duplicates, Sort Colors, move zeros, linked-list operations
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: In-place buffer compaction; zero-copy stream rewriting

patterns.name: Sliding window (variable)
patterns.recognitionCues: 'longest/shortest subarray/substring satisfying condition'; contiguous required
patterns.constraintTriggers: monotone feasibility must hold; n up to 10^5
patterns.coreIdea: Grow right pointer; shrink left while invalid. ONLY valid when extending cannot repair a violation.
patterns.dataStructures: hash map or count array for window contents, two indices
patterns.failureModes: Applying to non-monotone conditions (e.g. sum>=k with negatives); wrong shrink condition
patterns.canonicalExamples: Longest unique substring, minimum size subarray sum, fruit into baskets
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Rate limiting, windowed quotas, token bucket

patterns.name: Sliding window + counting
patterns.recognitionCues: 'at most K distinct','replace at most k characters','subarrays with exactly k'
patterns.constraintTriggers: alphabet/cardinality bounded; n up to 10^5
patterns.coreIdea: Track frequency inside the window; exactly(K) = atMost(K) - atMost(K-1)
patterns.dataStructures: hash map, freq array, maxFreq variable
patterns.failureModes: Recomputing maxFreq on every shrink; wrong atMost monotonicity assumption
patterns.canonicalExamples: Longest repeating character replacement, K different integers, permutation in string
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Cardinality-bounded caches; distinct-key windows in streaming analytics

patterns.name: Binary search (index)
patterns.recognitionCues: sorted array; 'first/last position'; 'O(log n) required'
patterns.constraintTriggers: sorted, or search space has a monotone property; n up to 10^7
patterns.coreIdea: Maintain a half-open invariant (lo<=answer<hi); shrink systematically; no templates
patterns.dataStructures: sorted array (or implicit sorted space)
patterns.failureModes: Off-by-one errors; lo<hi vs lo<=hi confusion; infinite loops; wrong mid formula
patterns.canonicalExamples: Binary search, first/last position, find minimum in rotated array
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: SSTable lookups, sorted offset indexes, version search

patterns.name: Binary search on answer
patterns.recognitionCues: 'minimize the maximum','maximize the minimum','minimum capacity/speed/time'; large answer range
patterns.constraintTriggers: answer <= 10^9, predicate check is O(n) or O(n log n)
patterns.coreIdea: Search the ANSWER SPACE with a monotone feasible(x) predicate; 3 validity conditions must hold
patterns.dataStructures: feasibility predicate function + binary search loop
patterns.failureModes: Non-monotone predicate; wrong search bounds; predicate accidentally O(n^2)
patterns.canonicalExamples: Koko eating bananas, ship packages, split array, min days for bouquets
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Capacity planning, autoscaling, SLO fitting, quota allocation

patterns.name: Sort + linear scan (preprocessing)
patterns.recognitionCues: 'intervals','pairs','sorted input assumed'; O(n log n) acceptable
patterns.constraintTriggers: n up to 10^5, no online queries
patterns.coreIdea: Sorting creates a monotonicity you can then exploit with a single greedy pass
patterns.dataStructures: sort + one or two pointers or a heap
patterns.failureModes: Wrong sort key (start vs end vs value); assuming stability; sorting when a heap suffices
patterns.canonicalExamples: Merge intervals, non-overlapping intervals, sort colors, meeting rooms
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Log compaction ordering, sorted shard merging, LSM-tree compaction

patterns.name: Interval / sweep line
patterns.recognitionCues: 'overlapping intervals','maximum concurrent events','resources needed at peak'
patterns.constraintTriggers: intervals, events with timestamps; n up to 10^5
patterns.coreIdea: Convert intervals to +1/-1 events and sweep; or maintain a min-heap of active end times
patterns.dataStructures: sorted events array, min-heap of end times
patterns.failureModes: Tie-breaking between end and start at the same time; off-by-one on closed intervals
patterns.canonicalExamples: Meeting rooms II, car pooling, calendar, task scheduler
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Concurrent resource counting (GPU/CPU slots), admission control

patterns.name: Monotonic stack
patterns.recognitionCues: 'next greater/smaller element','previous smaller','span','largest rectangle'
patterns.constraintTriggers: array; n up to 10^5
patterns.coreIdea: Keep a monotone stack; each pop resolves one answer; total pops <= n  ->  amortized O(n)
patterns.dataStructures: stack of indices (not values)
patterns.failureModes: Storing values not indices; equal-element double counting; missing sentinel flush at end
patterns.canonicalExamples: Daily temperatures, next greater element, largest rectangle in histogram, subarray minimums
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Monotone-break detection in metric streams, backpressure onset

patterns.name: Monotonic deque
patterns.recognitionCues: 'maximum/minimum of every window of size k','sliding extremum','windowed DP'
patterns.constraintTriggers: fixed or bounded window; n up to 10^6
patterns.coreIdea: Maintain a deque of indices in monotone order; evict out-of-window and dominated candidates
patterns.dataStructures: deque of indices
patterns.failureModes: Not evicting expired indices; storing values not indices; wrong eviction order
patterns.canonicalExamples: Sliding window maximum, jump game VI, constrained subsequence sum
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Rolling max latency, watermarks, windowed DP in schedulers

patterns.name: Heap / top-K / streaming extremum
patterns.recognitionCues: 'k largest/smallest','median of stream','schedule next available resource'
patterns.constraintTriggers: k<<n or online data; n up to 10^6
patterns.coreIdea: Partial order is enough; a heap gives the extreme in O(log n); heapify is O(n)
patterns.dataStructures: min-heap or max-heap; two heaps for median; heap of (key, cursor) for merge
patterns.failureModes: Full sort when k is tiny; wrong polarity; not using lazy deletion for stale entries
patterns.complexity: O(n log k) or O(log n) per operation
patterns.canonicalExamples: Kth largest, k closest, find median from stream, merge k sorted lists, task scheduler
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Top-K hot keys, p99 estimation, eviction candidate selection, priority scheduling

patterns.name: Greedy invariants
patterns.recognitionCues: 'maximum number of','minimum steps','locally safe choice'; often after sorting
patterns.constraintTriggers: exchange argument must hold; usually O(n log n)
patterns.coreIdea: Prove by exchange or staying-ahead that the local choice is in some optimal solution
patterns.dataStructures: sort + counters, heap, or simple scan
patterns.failureModes: Unproven greedy; missing a counterexample that breaks it; using greedy where DP is required
patterns.canonicalExamples: Jump game II, gas station, partition labels, refueling stops
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Admission control, retry budgets, checkpoint placement

patterns.name: Design / structure composition
patterns.recognitionCues: 'implement X with O(1) get/put/delete','LRU','LFU','getRandom'
patterns.constraintTriggers: operation TC is the spec; n up to 10^5 ops
patterns.coreIdea: Compose two structures so each required operation is O(1)/O(log n); API dictates structures
patterns.dataStructures: hash map + doubly linked list (LRU), freq buckets + maps (LFU), array + index map (getRandom)
patterns.failureModes: Choosing structures by habit not by API; forgetting to keep both structures in sync on every path
patterns.canonicalExamples: LRU cache, LFU cache, RandomizedSet, TimeMap, hit counter
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Page/feature/embedding caches, KV stores, rate limiters, versioned stores

patterns.name: Bit manipulation
patterns.recognitionCues: 'subset of at most 20 items','XOR','without extra space','count bits','feature flags'
patterns.constraintTriggers: n<=20 for subset enumeration; 32/64-bit word for bit tricks
patterns.coreIdea: A bitmask is a tiny set with O(1) set operations; XOR cancels pairs; use popcount for size
patterns.dataStructures: integer masks, popcount, __builtin_ctz
patterns.failureModes: Signed right-shifts; operator precedence bugs (use parentheses); overflow on mask<<1
patterns.complexity: O(1) per mask op; O(2^n) for full enumeration
patterns.canonicalExamples: Single number II, sum without +, missing number, subset enumeration
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Bitmaps, feature flags, GPU lane/warp masks, bloom filter ops

patterns.name: Tree recursion (contract-first)
patterns.recognitionCues: 'depth','balanced','path sum','subtree property','lowest common ancestor'
patterns.constraintTriggers: n up to 10^5; beware recursion depth on skewed trees
patterns.coreIdea: Define exactly what the function returns for a subtree; write it in English before coding; then trust it
patterns.dataStructures: recursion, call stack, optional memoisation
patterns.failureModes: Vague contracts; mixing 'answer' with 'return value'; stack overflow on skewed trees
patterns.canonicalExamples: Depth, balanced, diameter, max path sum, LCA, validate BST
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Recursive dependency evaluation, nested config resolution

patterns.name: Tree DP (post-order)
patterns.recognitionCues: 'max path','rob houses in tree','distribute coins','max sum with no adjacent'
patterns.constraintTriggers: tree, single-pass wanted
patterns.coreIdea: Combine children's return values at the parent; return one value upward; update global answer separately
patterns.dataStructures: recursion + tuple return (gain upward, answer updated)
patterns.failureModes: Returning the global answer upward; double-counting the root node; forgetting to clamp negatives
patterns.canonicalExamples: Diameter, max path sum, house robber III, distribute coins
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Aggregating metrics up a topology/ownership tree

patterns.name: BST ordering
patterns.recognitionCues: 'validate BST','k-th smallest in BST','BST range queries'
patterns.constraintTriggers: BST given, may be unbalanced
patterns.coreIdea: In-order traversal is sorted; propagate valid range (lo, hi) top-down instead of comparing parent-child
patterns.dataStructures: recursion with range bounds, iterative inorder stack
patterns.failureModes: Comparing only parent-child (misses deep violations); ignoring duplicate policy
patterns.canonicalExamples: Validate BST, kth smallest, insert/delete, range queries
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Ordered indexes, range scans, B-tree node invariants

patterns.name: BFS levels / shortest hops
patterns.recognitionCues: 'minimum steps','level order','nearest X','spread from source'
patterns.constraintTriggers: unweighted graph or grid; n up to 10^5
patterns.coreIdea: First visit = shortest distance; seed all sources at level 0 for multi-source; expand in layers
patterns.dataStructures: queue, visited set/array
patterns.failureModes: Marking visited on pop (causes exponential blowup); mixing level boundaries
patterns.canonicalExamples: Rotting oranges, word ladder, open the lock, right side view, 01-matrix
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Hop counts, blast-radius analysis, BFS-based propagation

patterns.name: Graph DFS / components
patterns.recognitionCues: 'islands','connected components','clone graph','cycle detection','safe states'
patterns.constraintTriggers: grid or adjacency list; n up to 10^5
patterns.coreIdea: Explore exhaustively; component identity or cycle colour (white/grey/black) is the output
patterns.dataStructures: recursion or explicit stack, visited array, colour array for directed cycles
patterns.failureModes: Recursion depth on large grids; not handling multiple components; directed vs undirected cycle logic
patterns.canonicalExamples: Number of islands, clone graph, find eventual safe states, course schedule
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Topology discovery, cluster membership, service-graph crawling

patterns.name: Union Find (DSU)
patterns.recognitionCues: 'connected components that grow','merge groups','edges arrive incrementally','redundant edge'
patterns.constraintTriggers: n up to 10^6; many merges and find queries
patterns.coreIdea: Maintain disjoint sets with path compression + union by size for near-O(1) amortized ops
patterns.dataStructures: parent array + size array
patterns.failureModes: Forgetting BOTH optimizations; using DSU where order of nodes matters; O(n) find without compression
patterns.canonicalExamples: Number of provinces, accounts merge, redundant connection, dynamic connectivity
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Cluster membership, shard grouping, entity dedup, dynamic edge-stream connectivity

patterns.name: Topological sorting
patterns.recognitionCues: 'prerequisites','build order','dependency resolution','detect cycle in directed graph'
patterns.constraintTriggers: DAG (or detect if not); V+E up to 10^5
patterns.coreIdea: Remove in-degree-0 nodes repeatedly (Kahn); or DFS with 3 colours; cycle = fewer than n emitted
patterns.dataStructures: in-degree array + queue (Kahn), or recursion + colour array (DFS)
patterns.failureModes: Not detecting cycles; assuming a unique ordering exists; skipping isolated nodes
patterns.canonicalExamples: Course schedule I/II, alien dictionary, task order, build systems
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: DAG job scheduling, ML pipeline orchestration, build dependency resolution

patterns.name: Dijkstra / weighted shortest path
patterns.recognitionCues: 'minimum cost/time path','non-negative edge weights','network delay'
patterns.constraintTriggers: weights >= 0; E up to 10^5
patterns.coreIdea: Greedily finalize the closest unfinished node; the popped distance is final (non-negative weights only)
patterns.dataStructures: min-heap of (distance, node) + dist array
patterns.failureModes: Using on negative weights; not skipping stale heap entries; wrong objective (min-max vs min-sum)
patterns.canonicalExamples: Network delay, path with max probability, min effort, cheapest flights
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Latency-aware routing, cost-based placement, weighted service graphs

patterns.name: State-space BFS/Dijkstra
patterns.recognitionCues: 'minimum moves with a resource budget','compound state','configuration reachability'
patterns.constraintTriggers: state space bounded and enumerable; states up to ~10^6
patterns.coreIdea: Nodes are FULL STATES (not just position); encode the state tuple; visited keyed on the complete state
patterns.dataStructures: queue or min-heap, visited set of encoded state tuples
patterns.failureModes: Visited keyed on partial state (silent wrong answer); unbounded state space; expensive encoding
patterns.canonicalExamples: Sliding puzzle, obstacle elimination, open the lock, minimum genetic mutation
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Scheduler/config state exploration, rollout planning, deployment state machines

patterns.name: Backtracking + pruning
patterns.recognitionCues: 'all combinations/permutations/partitions','place N items with constraints'
patterns.constraintTriggers: n small (<=20) or with heavy pruning; exponential in theory
patterns.coreIdea: Choose, explore, unchoose; the real skill is pruning branches that cannot lead to valid solutions
patterns.dataStructures: recursion, path array, bitmasks for O(1) constraint checks
patterns.failureModes: No pruning; incorrect dedup; mutating shared state without restoring it
patterns.canonicalExamples: Subsets, permutations, N-Queens, sudoku, palindrome partitioning, word search
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Config search, placement under conflict constraints, hyperparameter enumeration

patterns.name: Trie / prefix tree
patterns.recognitionCues: 'prefix queries','dictionary of words','autocomplete','search with wildcards'
patterns.constraintTriggers: alphabet size small (<=26); many words/queries
patterns.coreIdea: Share prefixes to make prefix queries proportional to word length; enables DFS pruning
patterns.dataStructures: trie nodes (array or hash map per node) with end flags
patterns.failureModes: Memory blowup on large alphabets; using a trie where a hashset is simpler and sufficient
patterns.canonicalExamples: Implement trie, word search II, add and search words, longest prefix match
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Autocomplete, tokenizer vocabularies, longest-prefix-match routing

patterns.name: DP (1D state design)
patterns.recognitionCues: 'number of ways','min/max cost','can we reach target','decisions at each step'
patterns.constraintTriggers: n up to 10^5; clear stages or positions
patterns.coreIdea: Define state  ->  transition  ->  base case  ->  evaluation order  ->  answer location (in that exact order)
patterns.dataStructures: 1D array or hash map
patterns.failureModes: Defining transition before state; wrong evaluation order; reading answer from wrong position
patterns.canonicalExamples: Climbing stairs, house robber, decode ways, jump game, coin change
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Stage-wise cost optimisation, pipeline configuration selection

patterns.name: DP (knapsack family)
patterns.recognitionCues: 'subset sum','choose items under capacity budget','coin change','ways to make amount'
patterns.constraintTriggers: capacity/sum bounded (pseudo-polynomial); n * capacity <= 10^7
patterns.coreIdea: Capacity is a DP dimension; loop order encodes 0/1 (descending) vs unbounded (ascending)
patterns.dataStructures: 1D or 2D DP arrays
patterns.failureModes: Wrong loop order; counting permutations vs combinations; not handling 0-capacity base case
patterns.canonicalExamples: Partition equal subset, coin change I/II, ones and zeroes, target sum
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Memory/GPU packing, multi-resource quota allocation

patterns.name: DP (two sequences)
patterns.recognitionCues: 'two strings','edit distance','common subsequence','interleaving'
patterns.constraintTriggers: m, n up to ~1000
patterns.coreIdea: dp[i][j] over prefixes of both sequences; derive transitions from the problem definition
patterns.dataStructures: 2D array or rolling 1D for space optimization
patterns.failureModes: Index confusion (i=0 means empty prefix); wrong base cases; optimizing space before correctness
patterns.complexity: O(mn) time, O(min(m,n)) space with rolling
patterns.canonicalExamples: LCS, edit distance, interleaving strings, distinct subsequences
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Diffing, log/sequence alignment, tokenizer alignment

patterns.name: DP (interval)
patterns.recognitionCues: 'optimal order of operations on a range','merge/burst/remove from a subarray'
patterns.constraintTriggers: n up to ~500 (O(n^3) acceptable)
patterns.coreIdea: Solve shorter ranges first; pick the LAST operation (not first) to keep subproblems independent
patterns.dataStructures: 2D DP array dp[left][right]
patterns.failureModes: Picking the first operation instead of the last; wrong iteration order (must go by length)
patterns.canonicalExamples: Burst balloons, longest palindromic subsequence, matrix chain, minimum cost to merge stones
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Optimal chunking, merge ordering, compaction cost minimisation

patterns.name: DP (bitmask)
patterns.recognitionCues: 'n<=20','visit all nodes','assign items to groups','travelling salesman variant'
patterns.constraintTriggers: n<=20 (2^n states must fit in memory)
patterns.coreIdea: State includes a subset bitmask; transition adds one element; (mask, position) is the full state
patterns.dataStructures: dp[mask][...] arrays
patterns.failureModes: Not recognising the n<=20 signal; state explosion; recomputing popcount in the inner loop
patterns.canonicalExamples: Shortest path visiting all nodes, matchsticks to square, assignment, TSP-variants
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Job-to-machine assignment, small-scale optimal placement

patterns.name: DP optimization (deque/heap in transition)
patterns.recognitionCues: naive DP transition is O(nk) or O(n^2) and n>10^3
patterns.constraintTriggers: tight time limit + large n
patterns.coreIdea: Optimize the transition by hiding a sliding-window maximum/minimum (monotonic deque) inside it
patterns.dataStructures: DP array + monotonic deque or heap or prefix max array
patterns.failureModes: Optimizing before the naive recurrence is correct and verified; breaking the window bound
patterns.canonicalExamples: Jump game VI, constrained subsequence sum, LIS in O(n log n)
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Streaming DP with bounded lookback; windowed online decisions

patterns.name: Fenwick Tree (BIT)
patterns.recognitionCues: 'mutable range sum','inversion count','point update + prefix query'
patterns.constraintTriggers: values coordinate-compressed; n up to 10^6
patterns.coreIdea: Lowest set bit (i & -i) tree decomposition; O(log n) update and query with tiny constant factor
patterns.dataStructures: 1D array (1-indexed)
patterns.failureModes: 0-indexing off-by-one; using when range updates needed without difference array
patterns.canonicalExamples: Range sum query, smaller numbers after self, reverse pairs
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: High-frequency telemetry counters, rolling latency meters

patterns.name: Segment Tree (range query)
patterns.recognitionCues: 'range min/max/sum/gcd query','point or range updates'; associative function
patterns.constraintTriggers: array size n up to 5 * 10^5, associative operator
patterns.coreIdea: Divide-and-conquer binary tree over array intervals; 4n array representation; lazy propagation
patterns.dataStructures: tree array, lazy array
patterns.failureModes: Size 2n instead of 4n; forgetting push_down before inspecting children; non-associative ops
patterns.canonicalExamples: Skyline, falling squares, range module, calendar booking
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Distributed SLA monitoring, physical memory reservation maps

patterns.name: Tarjan's DFS (bridges & SCC)
patterns.recognitionCues: 'critical connections','single point of failure','strongly connected components'
patterns.constraintTriggers: directed or undirected graph, O(V + E) target
patterns.coreIdea: Discovery time tin[u] and lowest ancestor low[u]; back-edge detection; condensation DAG
patterns.dataStructures: tin array, low array, visited stack
patterns.failureModes: Updating low[u] from parent edge in undirected graph; not popping stack up to u in SCC
patterns.canonicalExamples: Critical connections, graph disconnect, condensation DAG
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Fault-domain isolation, deadlock detection, build dependency validation

patterns.name: Hardware / Cache calibration
patterns.recognitionCues: high throughput, 10M+ QPS, low latency SLO, memory-constrained traversal
patterns.constraintTriggers: CPU cache line 64 bytes, DRAM access 60ns vs L1 1ns
patterns.coreIdea: Structure data contiguously (AOS vs SOA); eliminate pointer chasing; size blocks to L1/L2 cache
patterns.dataStructures: flat contiguous buffers, cyclic arrays
patterns.failureModes: Using linked lists / pointer trees in hot paths; ignoring false sharing and cache-line bouncing
patterns.canonicalExamples: Matrix transposition, ring buffers, flat hash tables
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Tensor memory layouts, GPU shared memory tiling, low-latency trading

patterns.name: High-performance hashing
patterns.recognitionCues: zero tail-latency, low collision variance, predictable lookup time
patterns.constraintTriggers: in-memory key-value store, load factor 0.8 - 0.9
patterns.coreIdea: Robin Hood displacement or Cuckoo two-table hashing; bounded worst-case probe lengths
patterns.dataStructures: flat key/value array + probe count byte
patterns.failureModes: Infinite loops during cuckoo cycles without stash; bad hash functions
patterns.canonicalExamples: In-memory KV store, RocksDB cache, Swiss table
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Storage engine block caches, Memcached, Redis hash tables

patterns.name: Adaptive Cache (ARC)
patterns.recognitionCues: dynamic workload with mixed scans and recurring loops; hit ratio optimization
patterns.constraintTriggers: fixed cache memory budget c
patterns.coreIdea: Balance recency (T1) and frequency (T2) dynamically using ghost history lists (B1, B2)
patterns.dataStructures: 4 LRU lists (T1, T2, B1, B2) + hash map
patterns.failureModes: Losing ghost entries on eviction; incorrect target size p boundary clipping [0, c]
patterns.canonicalExamples: ZFS storage ARC, buffer pool management, LLM prompt cache
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Database buffer managers, kernel page caches, multi-tenant AI caching

patterns.name: Lock-free ring buffer
patterns.recognitionCues: high-speed inter-thread message passing; zero lock contention; producer-consumer
patterns.constraintTriggers: single producer single consumer (SPSC) or MPMC; power-of-two size
patterns.coreIdea: Head and tail indices advancing monotonically; masking with (size - 1); cache line padding (64 bytes)
patterns.dataStructures: atomic size_t head, tail; contiguous array buffer
patterns.failureModes: False sharing between head and tail; missing memory barriers (acquire/release); ABA problem in MPMC
patterns.canonicalExamples: Circular queue, circular deque, bounded blocking queue
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: LMAX Disruptor, GPU command rings, high-throughput network packet ingestion

patterns.name: HNSW graph search
patterns.recognitionCues: approximate nearest neighbor (ANN), vector similarity, high dimensionality (d=128 to 1536)
patterns.constraintTriggers: dataset N up to 10^8 vectors, query latency < 5ms
patterns.coreIdea: Multi-layer proximity graph (skip-list concept); greedy routing on coarse upper layers, beam search on layer 0
patterns.dataStructures: layered adjacency list, candidate priority queue, visited set
patterns.failureModes: Local minima traps with too small efSearch; cyclic graph infinite loops without visited filter
patterns.canonicalExamples: Vector embeddings, multimodal search, semantic retrieval
patterns.aiInfraRelevance: Vector databases (Milvus, Pinecone, Qdrant, FAISS), RAG pipelines

cards.triggerCue: 'count subarrays with sum = k' + negatives present  ->  window fails
cards.coreIdea: hash map prefix -> count; store what you've seen; look up (prefix - k)
cards.complexity: O(n) time O(n) space: one pass, O(1) map ops
cards.invariant: Sliding window fails with negatives (non-monotone). Use prefix+count map.
cards.failureTrap: F11: tries sliding window; fails because negatives break monotonicity
cards.variants: Return the longest such subarray; 2D version; sum divisible by k
cards.anchorCue: Contiguous + sum + negatives = prefix hash, not window

cards.triggerCue: 'minimum window containing all characters of t'
cards.coreIdea: need/have counters + two pointers; expand right, shrink left when have==need
cards.invariant: When 'have' increments (only when freq goes from need-1 to need); shrink while valid
cards.failureTrap: F6: recomputes the whole counter check each step  ->  O(n^2)
cards.variants: Multiple pattern strings; window over a stream; minimum window subsequence
cards.anchorCue: Shortest valid window = expand right first, shrink left aggressively

cards.triggerCue: 'minimum speed such that all piles eaten within h hours'
cards.coreIdea: feasible(speed) = all(ceil(p/speed) for p in piles) <= h; monotone decreasing as speed grows
cards.invariant: feasible(x) is monotone: if x works, x+1 also works
cards.failureTrap: F3: tries greedy or average; doesn't see the monotone predicate
cards.variants: Non-integer speeds; per-pile costs; maximize instead of minimize
cards.anchorCue: 'minimum X such that condition holds' = BS on answer

cards.triggerCue: 'largest rectangle area under bars'
cards.coreIdea: maintain increasing-height stack of indices; on each pop, compute the rectangle using right-left-1
cards.complexity: O(n) amortized: each index pushed and popped exactly once
cards.invariant: Stack contains indices of bars in strictly increasing height order at all times
cards.failureTrap: F6: nested loops O(n^2); mishandles equal heights or the end-of-array flush
cards.variants: Maximal rectangle in binary matrix; 3D variant; sum of subarray minimums
cards.anchorCue: Need previous-smaller and next-smaller boundaries simultaneously = monotonic stack

cards.problem: LC 295 Find Median from Data Stream
cards.triggerCue: 'median of a stream' + online insertion
cards.coreIdea: max-heap for lower half + min-heap for upper half; rebalance so sizes differ by at most 1
cards.complexity: O(log n) insert, O(1) median query
cards.invariant: max-heap.size  in  {min-heap.size, min-heap.size+1} at all times; max-heap.top <= min-heap.top
cards.failureTrap: F3: re-sorts on every query; O(n log n) per call
cards.variants: Sliding-window median; arbitrary percentile; distributed streaming quantiles
cards.anchorCue: Online order statistic = two heaps or segment tree + BIT

cards.triggerCue: 'O(1) get and put with LRU eviction'
cards.coreIdea: hash map for O(1) lookup + doubly linked list for O(1) move-to-front and O(1) eviction from tail
cards.invariant: Most-recently-used node is always at head; least-recently-used is always at tail
cards.failureTrap: F4: uses array/list  ->  O(n) moves; or forgets to update the map on eviction
cards.variants: TTL eviction; thread-safe LRU; LFU; write-through/write-back
cards.anchorCue: O(1) ordered access = hash map + doubly linked list

cards.triggerCue: 'O(1) get and put with LFU eviction'
cards.coreIdea: freq -> OrderedDict bucket map + key -> (val,freq) map + minFreq pointer
cards.invariant: minFreq can only increase by 0 or 1 on an access; it resets to 1 on every put of a new key
cards.failureTrap: F3: scans for min frequency O(n); loses the minFreq invariant on edge cases
cards.variants: Aging/decay of counts; window LFU; hybrid ARC policy
cards.anchorCue: Frequency-ordered eviction = bucketed frequency lists with a minFreq pointer

cards.problem: LC 124 Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
cards.triggerCue: 'maximum path sum' where path can bend at any node
cards.coreIdea: at each node, return max(0, node.val + best_downward) for parent; update global answer with left+node+right
cards.invariant: Return value = best downward gain from this node; global answer = best bent path through this node
cards.failureTrap: F3: returns the bent path upward; forgets to clamp negative downward gains to 0
cards.variants: Path with at most k turns; count of maximum paths; k-ary tree variant
cards.anchorCue: Global answer updated at node != value returned to parent

cards.triggerCue: 'serialize a tree to a string and deserialize it back'
cards.coreIdea: preorder traversal + null markers; use a queue/index cursor during deserialization
cards.invariant: Every null must be explicitly encoded; the grammar determines unique decodability
cards.failureTrap: F1: improvises the format; cannot parse back an ambiguous encoding
cards.variants: N-ary tree; BST-optimized encoding (no nulls needed); compact binary format
cards.anchorCue: Define the grammar BEFORE writing code  ->  guaranteed decodability

cards.triggerCue: 'prerequisites exist','valid ordering required','detect cycle in directed graph'
cards.coreIdea: Kahn: maintain in-degree array + queue; emit when in-degree reaches 0; cycle if emitted < n
cards.invariant: In-degree-0 nodes are always safe to emit; the queue holds exactly the current safe-to-emit set
cards.failureTrap: F6: cannot detect cycles; assumes unique ordering
cards.variants: Lexicographically smallest order; parallel scheduling with k workers; critical path
cards.anchorCue: 'ordering with dependencies' = topological sort (Kahn or DFS-colours)

cards.triggerCue: 'minimum time for signal to reach all nodes' + non-negative weights
cards.coreIdea: standard Dijkstra; answer = max of all shortest distances; -1 if any node unreachable
cards.invariant: Once a node is popped from the min-heap, its distance is final (non-negative weights guarantee this)
cards.failureTrap: F3: uses plain BFS on weighted edges; or forgets to skip stale heap entries
cards.variants: Negative weights (use Bellman-Ford); k-hop limit (add hop dimension); multi-source
cards.anchorCue: Weighted min cost + non-negative weights = Dijkstra

cards.problem: LC 787 Cheapest Flights Within K Stops
cards.triggerCue: 'cheapest path with at most k stops' = extra constraint on path length
cards.coreIdea: dp[t][v] = min cost to reach v using at most t hops; iterate t from 1 to k+1
cards.complexity: O(k | E): k+1 rounds of edge relaxation
cards.invariant: Using exactly t hops distinguishes dp layers; copy previous layer before updating
cards.failureTrap: F3: runs plain Dijkstra and ignores the stop constraint; or modifies dist in-place breaking the layer
cards.variants: Exactly k stops; time windows; multiple path constraints
cards.anchorCue: Extra constraint on a path = add a state dimension (hops, resources, keys)

cards.problem: LC 1293 Shortest Path Grid with Obstacles
cards.triggerCue: 'minimum steps' + 'budget of k removals'
cards.coreIdea: BFS over state = (row, col, remaining_removals); visited is a 3D array
cards.invariant: The state is (position + resource); visited must include ALL components of the state
cards.failureTrap: F3: keys visited on (r,c) only  ->  finds a path but not necessarily the minimum (wrong answer silently)
cards.variants: Multiple resource budgets; weighted removals  ->  Dijkstra over states
cards.anchorCue: Budget/resource in problem = extra state dimension  ->  state-space search

cards.triggerCue: 'place n non-attacking queens on n*n board'
cards.coreIdea: recurse row by row; track occupied cols, main diags, anti-diags with bitmasks for O(1) conflict check
cards.invariant: At any partial placement, each attacked set is maintained incrementally (add on enter, remove on exit)
cards.failureTrap: F6: no incremental conflict tracking; rescans the board each step
cards.variants: Count only; n<=15 with bitmask DP; other piece types; hexagonal boards
cards.anchorCue: Constraint placement = backtracking with O(1) conflict checks via bitmasks

cards.triggerCue: 'longest strictly increasing subsequence'
cards.coreIdea: tails[i] = smallest tail of all LIS of length i+1; binary search to find insertion point
cards.complexity: O(n log n); naive DP is O(n^2)
cards.invariant: tails is always sorted; tails[i] is updated in place; it does NOT store an actual subsequence
cards.failureTrap: F3: confuses tails with an actual subsequence; or uses wrong bound (lower vs upper)
cards.variants: Count of LIS; 2D (envelopes); non-strict version; print one LIS
cards.anchorCue: Subsequence + order constraint = DP; optimize with patience sorting (tails + binary search)

cards.triggerCue: 'optimal order of removals from a range', 'multiply with neighbors'
cards.coreIdea: dp[l][r] = max coins when all balloons in (l,r) are burst; try each k as the LAST to burst in range
cards.invariant: The LAST balloon to burst in a range sees its left and right boundaries as fixed; subproblems are independent
cards.failureTrap: F3: picks the FIRST burst  ->  subproblems overlap; the key is reversing to think about the last operation
cards.variants: Merge stones; matrix chain; k-way merges; removing elements with range penalties
cards.anchorCue: Order-of-operations optimum = interval DP with 'last operation' framing

cards.problem: LC 847 Shortest Path Visiting All Nodes
cards.triggerCue: 'shortest path visiting all n nodes', n<=12
cards.coreIdea: BFS over state = (node, visited_mask); seed with all (node, 1<<node) states at distance 0
cards.invariant: n<=12 is the only signal needed: 2^1^2=4096 states * 12 nodes = trivially enumerable
cards.failureTrap: F2: misses the n<=12 constraint; tries shortest path ignoring the 'visit all' constraint
cards.variants: Weighted edges (Dijkstra over states); must return to start; k-of-n visits
cards.anchorCue: Tiny n + 'visit all' = bitmask state space

cards.triggerCue: 'maximum subsequence sum where index gap <= k'
cards.coreIdea: dp[i] = max(nums[i], max(dp[j] for j in [i-k, i-1]) + nums[i]); optimize with a deque max
cards.invariant: Deque maintains indices of maximum dp values in decreasing order; evict those outside [i-k, i-1]
cards.failureTrap: F5: writes O(nk) and times out; or optimizes before verifying correctness of the recurrence
cards.variants: Two-sided constraints; weighted gaps; streaming variant with a sliding window
cards.anchorCue: Sliding-window maximum hidden inside a DP transition = monotonic deque

cards.triggerCue: 'O(1) insert, delete, and uniform random element'
cards.coreIdea: array for O(1) random access + hash map (val -> index) for O(1) lookup; delete by swap-with-last
cards.invariant: After swap-with-last, update the moved element's index in the map; then pop the last element
cards.failureTrap: F4: uses a set  ->  cannot do O(1) uniform random sample
cards.variants: Duplicates allowed; weighted random; distributed sampling
cards.anchorCue: Uniform random + O(1) delete = array + index map (swap-with-last)

cards.triggerCue: 'split array into m parts to minimize the largest part sum'
cards.coreIdea: BS: feasible(mid) = can we split with each part <= mid?  -  greedy O(n); DP: dp[k][i]=min largest for k parts in A[i:]
cards.invariant: feasible(x) is monotone: if x works, x+1 also works; this is the key validity condition
cards.failureTrap: F3: jumps to DP and times out; or writes a non-monotone predicate
cards.variants: Return the actual split; k as a variable; weights; minimize sum of maximums
cards.anchorCue: 'Minimize the maximum' = binary search on answer + greedy feasibility check

cards.triggerCue: 'mutable array with dynamic range sum queries'
cards.coreIdea: binary tree over array intervals OR lowest-set-bit tree (i & -i); O(log n) update and query
cards.complexity: O(log n) update, O(log n) query
cards.invariant: Range sum in BIT: query(r) - query(l-1); Segment Tree: combine(left_child, right_child)
cards.failureTrap: F6: writes O(n) scan on query or O(n) rebuild on update; TLE on frequent updates
cards.variants: Range minimum/maximum query; lazy propagation for range updates; 2D Fenwick
cards.anchorCue: Mutable array + frequent range queries = Segment Tree or BIT

cards.problem: LC 1192 Critical Connections in a Network
cards.triggerCue: 'edges whose removal disconnects the graph (bridges)'
cards.coreIdea: DFS tracking discovery time tin[u] and lowest reachable ancestor low[u]; bridge if low[v] > tin[u]
cards.invariant: low[u] = min(low[u], tin[v]) for back-edges; low[u] = min(low[u], low[v]) for tree-edges
cards.failureTrap: F3: removes each edge and runs BFS O(E * (V+E)) -> TLE; forgets to skip parent edge in low calculation
cards.variants: Articulation points (cut vertices); strongly connected components (condensation DAG)
cards.anchorCue: Single point of failure / bridge edge = Tarjan tin/low DFS

cards.triggerCue: 'visit every directed edge exactly once in lexicographical order'
cards.coreIdea: Hierholzer's algorithm: post-order DFS with sorted adjacency lists; prepend to path on return
cards.complexity: O(E log E) due to sorting edges
cards.invariant: When current node has no outgoing edges, it must be the end of the Eulerian path; prepend to itinerary
cards.failureTrap: F6: greedy DFS gets stuck in dead ends without backtracking; does not reverse post-order traversal
cards.variants: De Bruijn sequence; DNA fragment reconstruction; network packet trace
cards.anchorCue: Visit all edges exactly once = Hierholzer Eulerian traversal

cards.problem: LC 28 Find First Occurrence in String
cards.triggerCue: 'find needle in haystack in linear time without backtracking'
cards.coreIdea: precompute prefix function pi[i] (longest proper prefix also a suffix); transition state machine
cards.invariant: pi[i] is the length of the longest proper prefix of s[0..i] that is also a suffix of s[0..i]
cards.failureTrap: F6: resets haystack pointer on mismatch -> O(N*M) worst case on repeating patterns
cards.variants: Aho-Corasick multi-pattern search; shortest palindrome prefix; cyclic shift check
cards.anchorCue: Linear string matching without backtracking = KMP prefix function

cards.triggerCue: 'cache workload with mixed sequential scans and recurring hot loops'
cards.coreIdea: four lists (T1 recent, T2 frequent, B1 ghost recent, B2 ghost frequent); adapt target size p
cards.complexity: O(1) per lookup, insertion, and eviction
cards.invariant: Total cache entries in T1 + T2 <= c; total ghost + active entries in T1 + T2 + B1 + B2 <= 2c
cards.failureTrap: F4: uses standard LRU; single sequential scan flushes all frequent pages out of memory
cards.variants: 2Q cache; Clock-Pro page replacement; LRFU with exponential decay
cards.anchorCue: Scan-resistant self-tuning caching = ARC 4-list architecture

cards.triggerCue: 'ultra-low latency producer-consumer message queue without mutexes'
cards.coreIdea: head and tail indices with power-of-two mask; cache-line padding (64 bytes); acquire-release semantics
cards.invariant: Buffer is full when (tail - head) == capacity; empty when tail == head; indices monotonically increase
cards.failureTrap: F10: places head and tail in the same cache line -> massive false sharing penalty; uses slow modulo
cards.variants: MPMC bounded queue; work-stealing deque; ring buffer stream compaction
cards.anchorCue: Wait-free single-producer single-consumer = padded lock-free ring buffer

cards.triggerCue: 'thread pool scheduler with private fast-path and concurrent stealing'
cards.coreIdea: owner pushes and pops LIFO at bottom (no CAS needed); thief workers steal FIFO at top with atomic CAS
cards.complexity: O(1) owner amortized, O(1) concurrent steal
cards.invariant: Owner operations bottom-- and bottom++ only synchronize with steal_top when bottom - top <= 1
cards.failureTrap: F6: synchronizes owner operations with global mutex; destroys parallel scalability
cards.variants: Go runtime scheduler; Tokio async runtime; Ray distributed execution engine
cards.anchorCue: Task pool with fast owner + concurrent steal = Chase-Lev Deque

cards.triggerCue: 'approximate nearest neighbor search on high-dimensional vectors in <5ms'
cards.coreIdea: hierarchical proximity graph; greedy search at top sparse layers; beam search on dense layer 0
cards.complexity: O(log N) query time, O(N * M) space
cards.invariant: At each layer, greedy step moves to neighbor closer to query; stops when no neighbor is strictly closer
cards.failureTrap: F3: uses KD-Tree for d=1536 -> degrades to O(N) exhaustive scan due to curse of dimensionality
cards.variants: IVF-PQ indexing; random projection trees (Annoy); ScaNN anisotropic vector quantization
cards.anchorCue: High-dimensional vector search = HNSW proximity graph navigation

cards.triggerCue: 'minimum time to complete all tasks with precedence constraints and task durations'
cards.coreIdea: topological sort computing longest path on DAG: dist[v] = max(dist[u] + time[v])
cards.invariant: dist[v] represents earliest finish time of course v; global answer is max(dist[v]) across all v
cards.failureTrap: F3: tries Dijkstra with shortest path; critical path is LONGEST path in a DAG
cards.variants: Memory-bounded operator scheduling; heterogeneous device placement; pipeline latency
cards.anchorCue: Precedence constraints + duration = Critical Path DAG scheduling

cards.triggerCue: 'estimate item frequencies and find top-K heavy hitters in sub-linear space'
cards.coreIdea: d x w 2D counter array with independent hash functions; Misra-Gries k-1 candidate pool
cards.complexity: O(1) per update, O(w * d) space
cards.invariant: Count-Min point estimate is min(C[i, h_i(x)]); Misra-Gries decrements all counts only when pool is full
cards.failureTrap: F4: stores all unique keys in hash map -> O(N) memory explosion on streaming big data
cards.variants: HyperLogLog cardinality; Bloom filter set membership; Reservoir sampling
cards.anchorCue: Streaming top-K and frequency in bounded space = Count-Min Sketch + Misra-Gries

readme.title: THE ONLY METRIC THAT MATTERS
readme.body:
Problem count is a lagging metric and a vanity number.
The metric that predicts interview success:
  * Time-to-pattern on UNLABELLED problems (target: <5 min for Medium by week 10)
  * Independent-solve rate (target: >70% by week 12)
  * Hint-dependency rate (target: <20% by week 10)
  * Ability to reconstruct any solved problem from memory 3 days later
Dashboard tracks all four. Fill it honestly or it becomes useless.

readme.title: DAILY BLOCK STRUCTURE  (1-2 hours total)
readme.body:
A) RETRIEVAL  [10-15 min]
   From memory, no notes: state yesterday's pattern trigger + invariant + complexity.
   If you cannot, add it to ReviewQueue immediately.

B) CONCEPT / TUTORIAL  [0-25 min  -  ONLY if DayPlan says YES]
   Read the DayPlan tutorial column. If it says NO, do not watch anything.
   The urge to watch a tutorial instead of struggling is a productivity trap.

C) DEEP SOLVING  [45-70 min  -  the real training block]
   Obey the STUCK PROTOCOL below. No shortcuts.

D) RECONSTRUCTION  [10 min]
   Close your solution. Open a blank file. Rebuild it from memory.
   If you cannot reconstruct it, you did not learn it.

E) FAILURE ANALYSIS  [5 min]
   Log every failure in FailureLog with an honest category + one preventive rule.

F) REVIEW  [10 min]
   Top item from ReviewQueue. Retrieval only  -  no re-reading.

readme.title: THE STUCK PROTOCOL  (non-negotiable, enforced in DayPlan column)
readme.body:
0-10 min   ->  NO help. Restate the problem in your own words.
              Write constraints. Write brute-force + its TC. Write target TC.
              Write 2-3 candidate approaches.

10-20 min  ->  ONE conceptual hint only. No code. No data-structure name if avoidable.
              Hint = a question that points you toward the right abstraction.

20-30 min  ->  Stronger hint: name the pattern or the key invariant.
              Still no implementation.

30+ min    ->  Read ONLY the core approach (2-3 sentences). Then close it.
              Implement entirely from scratch  -  never copy code.

If you read code  ->  problem is auto-logged as "Solution Viewed = Yes" and re-queued at +1 day.
If you solve with hints  ->  re-queued at +3 days, not +7.
The goal: "I understand WHY this solution exists." NOT "I understood it after being shown."

readme.title: PHASE SEQUENCE FOR EVERY IMPORTANT PROBLEM
readme.body:
1. UNDERSTAND   -  What is asked? What are constraints? What changes? What is reusable?
2. PREDICT       -  Write target TC from constraints. List 2-3 approaches. Name the bottleneck.
3. DERIVE        -  Attempt yourself. Use stuck protocol if needed.
4. IMPLEMENT     -  Write clean code.
5. ATTACK        -  Test: empty input, single element, all duplicates, max n, negatives, overflow, adversarial order.
6. OPTIMIZE      -  Can TC improve? If no, can SC improve? Is there a hidden invariant?
7. RECONSTRUCT   -  Close everything. Rebuild from memory and explain aloud.
8. SCHEDULE      -  ProblemDB auto-computes review dates based on your performance.

readme.title: TUTORIAL RULES  (35 curated tutorials across 168 days)
readme.body:
Watch BEFORE a problem only when the mental model is genuinely new (DayPlan marks these explicitly).
Do NOT watch because a specific problem is hard. Struggle first.
Watch AFTER only when you failed to recognise the SAME pattern twice.
Rewatch only if you cannot reconstruct the concept from memory.

For every tutorial, extract:
  * The TRIGGER (what wording in a problem should activate this pattern?)
  * The INVARIANT (what remains true throughout the algorithm?)
  * The COMPLEXITY ARGUMENT (why is it O(n)? O(n log n)?  -  derive it, do not accept it)

Do NOT memorise the presenter's code. That is passive consumption, not learning.

readme.title: FAILURE CATEGORIES  -  USE THESE CODES EVERYWHERE
readme.body:
F1-Understand    : misread or misunderstood the problem statement
F2-Pattern       : could not identify the correct pattern
F3-Derive        : knew the pattern, could not derive the approach
F4-WrongDS       : identified the right approach, chose the wrong data structure
F5-Complexity    : wrong or absent complexity analysis
F6-Implementation: correct approach, coding bug
F7-EdgeCase      : correct solution, missed an edge case
F8-Debugging     : took too long to find the bug
F9-Forgot        : knew this technique previously, forgot it
F10-Pressure     : failed specifically because of time pressure (fine in untimed)
F11-HintDependent: required a hint to make progress
F12-CantExplain  : could implement but could not explain the solution

readme.title: AUTO-ESCALATION RULES  (the plan adjusts to your failures)
readme.body:
If any category appears 3+ times in one week:
  F2 (Pattern)      ->  next week's 2 blind days must target that pattern family
                     + do 10 "name the pattern only" reps daily (5 min, no coding)
  F3 (Derive)       ->  add 1 extra reconstruction per day from the failed pattern
  F5 (Complexity)   ->  estimate TC out loud BEFORE every single problem  -  no exceptions
  F6 (Implement)    ->  write the invariant as a comment before every loop
  F7 (EdgeCase)     ->  run your personal edge-case checklist before every submission
  F10 (Pressure)    ->  replace one untimed day per week with a timed session
  F11 (HintDep)     ->  the stuck-protocol clock resets to 0  -  you must wait the full 30 min

If F2 or F3 each appear 5+ times in a single week: run a pattern-recognition drill session
(20 problems, no coding, just write "pattern: X" for each) before continuing the plan.

readme.title: MISSED DAYS  (no restarts, ever)
readme.body:
1 day missed      ->  resume exactly where you left off. Nothing special.
2-3 days missed   ->  RECOVERY SESSION: 15 min retrieval of last 3 patterns +
                    2 problems from top of ReviewQueue + nothing new.
1+ week missed    ->  MINI-DIAGNOSTIC: 3 unlabelled problems from the pool (60 min).
                    Re-enter the plan at the week whose patterns you failed.
                    Do NOT go back to Day 1. Do NOT do a multi-day catch-up pile.
                    Catch-up piles produce shallow results and break motivation.

readme.title: PRODUCTIVITY TRAPS  (re-read every Sunday)

* Watching tutorials instead of struggling
* Solving only easy problems
* Solving problems already labelled with the pattern (defeats the whole purpose)
* Reading the solution before 30 minutes are up
* Memorising templates instead of understanding invariants
* Copying code from solutions
* Doing 10 shallow solves instead of 3 deep ones
* Never revisiting problems (mastery requires forgetting and re-retrieving)
* Confusing recognition with mastery

Caching/eviction       ->  LRU, LFU, ARC (hashmap + ordered structure)
Scheduling             ->  heaps, topological order, priority queues
Dependency resolution  ->  DAG + Kahn's algorithm
Rate limiting          ->  sliding window, token bucket
Load balancing         ->  binary search on answer + greedy
Streaming metrics      ->  two heaps, monotonic deque, reservoir sampling
Sharding/partitioning  ->  hashing, consistent hashing, Union-Find
Indexing / search      ->  binary search, tries, sorted structures

Log merging            ->  k-way merge, interval merging

The interview DSA / infra DSA overlap is strongest in: heaps, hashing, graphs/DAGs,

readme.title: THE NVIDIA & GPU-SYSTEMS INTERVIEW STANDARD
readme.body:
NVIDIA does NOT interview like standard web/app Big Tech.
Interviewers in CUDA, TensorRT, Triton, NCCL, Tegra, Drivers, and AI Infrastructure
test whether your mental model matches the underlying SILICON.

1. HARDWARE-AWARE COMPLEXITY (Big-O in a vacuum is rejected):
   * Cache Lines: CPU/GPU memory moves in 64-byte or 128-byte chunks.
     A pointer-chasing O(N) linked-list is 50x slower than a contiguous O(N) array due to cache misses.
   * Memory Coalescing & Bank Conflicts: Consecutive threads must access consecutive
     memory addresses. Strided access serializes memory transactions into separate bus requests.
   * Branch Divergence: If threads in a 32-thread warp take different branches (if/else),
     both execution paths are serialized. Write branchless / bit-predicated logic where possible.

2. BITWISE ARITHMETIC AS A NATIVE LANGUAGE:
   * Thread & Warp Masks: __activemask(), __ballot_sync(), popcount (__builtin_popcount).
   * Memory Alignment: Aligning address X to 64 bytes: (X + 63) & ~63.
   * Fast Power-of-Two: (n & (n - 1)) == 0, modulo mask (x & (2^k - 1)).
   * Bit-reversal and lowest set bit (x & -x) for Fenwick trees and parallel FFTs.

3. PARALLEL REDUCTIONS & WARP PRIMITIVES:
   * Never stop at a sequential loop. Always be prepared to answer:
     "How does this run across 32 parallel threads in a warp?"
   * Master Blelloch work-efficient parallel scan (up-sweep / down-sweep tree reduction).
   * Master warp-shuffle reductions (__shfl_down_sync) for sum, min, max without shared memory.

4. DATA LAYOUT: SoA vs AoS:
   * Structure of Arrays (SoA: x[N], y[N], z[N]) allows SIMD/GPU coalesced vector loads.
   * Array of Structures (AoS: struct Point{x,y,z} pts[N]) causes strided, uncoalesced memory fetches.

5. LOCK-FREE COMMAND QUEUES & PRODUCER-CONSUMER:
   * SPSC (Single-Producer Single-Consumer) ring buffers with acquire/release memory fences.
   * Power-of-two buffer sizing for branchless index wrapping.
   * Avoid false sharing by padding cache lines (alignas(64)).

6. SPARSE MATRICES & TENSOR STRIDES:
   * Compressed Sparse Row (CSR: values, column_indices, row_pointers) and CSC.
   * 2:4 Structured Sparsity (NVIDIA Ampere/Hopper Tensor Core 2x throughput).
   * Strided indexing (offset = sum(coord[i] * stride[i])) and in-place tensor transposition.

7. NCCL & DISTRIBUTED COLLECTIVES:
   * Ring All-Reduce vs Tree All-Reduce: bandwidth vs latency trade-offs.
   * Ring All-Reduce: 2*(P-1)/P * S transfer size (constant bandwidth scaling as cluster size P grows).

readme.title: COMPLEXITY TRAINING  (first-class skill)
readme.body:
For EVERY problem, answer these before writing a single line of code:
  1. What is the brute-force TC and why?
  2. What makes it slow? (which step is repeated unnecessarily?)
  3. What is the target TC? (derived from n in the constraints)
  4. What is the likely lower bound? (can we prove nothing faster exists?)
  5. What is the SC?
  6. What happens at maximum input size? (n=10^5, n=10^9)

n <= 20        ->  O(2^n) or O(n!) acceptable (backtracking, bitmask DP)
n <= 500       ->  O(n^2) or O(n^2 log n) acceptable
n <= 5,000     ->  O(n^2) tight
n <= 100,000   ->  O(n log n) required
n <= 1,000,000 ->  O(n) strongly preferred
n <= 10^9      ->  O(log n) or O(1) only

nvidiaPlaybook.killerDialogue: Theoretically, this is O(N) time and O(N) space. However, in high-performance GPU systems or low-level CUDA kernels, instead of a pointer-based tree or linked list, I would lay this out in a contiguous 1D array (Structure of Arrays) aligned to 64-byte boundaries.
